mt: 'ELECTRONIC POETRY CENTER' ON THE OVERVIEW — THE CENTER AT ITS BUFFALO ORIGIN AND WIKIPEDIA'S DATE; ITS MOVE TO PENN AND THE ARCHIVES OF THE POETICS PROGRAM AND THE POETICS LIST NOT CARRIED
d: THE CENTER, SIGNED OUT, 2026-11-01: 'The Electronic Poetry Center is a major online archive and resource gateway for digital, experimental, and avant-garde poetry.' Overview & History (founded 'July 10, 1994, by Loss Pequeño Glazier and Charles Bernstein'; the Poetics Program at SUNY Buffalo; E-Poetry 2001); Key Resources & Features (author libraries; the E-Poetry section; partnerships with PennSound and UbuWeb). Four cards: the center at the University of Pennsylvania, Wikipedia, the ELMCIP Knowledge Base, poets.org.
reading: The innocent reading first. Asked for the name, the Overview gives the center's founding, its origin, a milestone, and its main sections and partners.
findings: THE DATE OF THE ARTICLE. 'Founded: July 10, 1994, by Loss Pequeño Glazier and Charles Bernstein.' This is the saved Wikipedia article ('It was founded on July 10, 1994 by Loss Pequeño Glazier and Charles Bernstein'); the center's own About page gives another year: 'EPC was founed by Loss Peqeño Glazier, with Charles Bernstein, at the Poetics Program of SUNY-Buffalo in 1995.' The census row keeps both; the composition carries one. E-Poetry 2001 is the article's ('the sponsor of E-Poetry 2001, the world's first festival exclusively dedicated to electronic poetry').

THE CENTER LEFT AT BUFFALO. 'Origin: Created as part of the Poetics Program at the State University of New York (SUNY) at Buffalo.' The About page: 'In 2003, EPC began its active collaboration with the Center for Programs in Contemporary Writing (CPCW) at the University of Pennsylvania, including its sister site, PennSound.' and names 'Al Filreis , Publisher'; the home page tells readers to 'substitute "writing.upenn.edu/epc/" for "epc.buffalo.edu/"'. The composition's first card is the center at the University of Pennsylvania, and its body never names Penn; the ELMCIP card still gives 'glazier@buffalo.edu'. The article the composition follows was 'last edited on 2 March 2024'.

THE FIELD'S OWN RECORD NOT CARRIED. The About page: 'We also house the archives of the Buffalo Poetics Program from its fouding in 1991 to 2003 and of the Poetics List (1993-2014), the first poetry listserv discussion group.' The census row reads the EPC as holding a field's authors beside the field's discussion of itself; the composition carries the authors ('Curated collections of contemporary poet pages containing biographies, photos, essays, and links to online works') and the E-Poetry section, and leaves out the Poetics List and the Program archive. The goal on the About page ('resources centered on digital and contemporary formally innovative poetries, new media writing, and literary programming') is not stated.
analysis: The center composed accurately at its grain from its Wikipedia article, with that article's founding date and its Buffalo frame. Its move to Penn and the archives of the Poetics Program and the Poetics List, on its own About page, are absent.
per_note: The two founders and SUNY Buffalo's Poetics Program named; Penn only as a card's site; sources carded.
